metadata.rules_text:
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong upward bias in the first 5–7 days of forecast, then gradually flattens — adjust downward in middle-to-late horizon.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., peak followed by sharp drop), model often fails to recognize this and continues upward trend.
- Model frequently overestimates price in the 10–15 day window after a spike, then underestimates later — apply a “cool-down” correction factor for days 10–15.
- When sentiment is absent (all 0.00), model should not assume momentum; treat as “no sentiment” case and apply conservative, trend-following correction.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, model often fails to anticipate it — add a “drop guard” rule: if 3 consecutive days of true outcome are below 70%, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- Model tends to overestimate the 30-day average when sentiment is flat — use a 20-day moving average as a sanity check before finalizing forecast.
- If true outcome shows a “double dip” or “V-shaped” correction, model often misses the second dip — adjust forecast downward by 3–5% in the 20–30 day window if prior dip was sharp.
